subject: Risk & Compliance
title: The 2008 Global Financial Crisis
description: A 60-second lesson on The 2008 Global Financial Crisis.

hook.text: Lehman Brothers collapses on September 15, 2008. Global credit freezes. The world economy nearly dies.

buildup.text: Subprime mortgages were packaged into complex securities sold globally. When borrowers defaulted, the system crumbled.

discovery.text: Interconnected banks meant one failure cascaded everywhere. The crisis wiped out $2 trillion in global economic output.

twist.text: Rating agencies gave toxic mortgage securities AAA ratings. The watchdogs enabled the crisis they should have prevented.

climax.text: The 2008 crisis exposed systemic risk: when everything is connected, one failure threatens everything.

punchline.text: Bad mortgages. AAA ratings. Systemic collapse. $2 trillion gone.

quiz.question: What role did rating agencies play in the 2008 crisis?
options: They gave AAA ratings to toxic mortgage securities
They correctly warned investors about risks
They had no involvement in the crisis
